page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, providing 32 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score, fall into the bottom 25% tier, reflecting the moderate clock speed of the underlying Intel Xeon architecture. Single-threaded gzip compression is particularly low, ranking in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core, consistently achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth is stable, with uncached read speeds at 98.84 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 48.76 GB/sec, both placing in the middle 50% of tested systems.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-threaded compute performance. The 256.0 GB RAM capacity supports in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and moderate database operations. It is also capable of handling medium-sized language model inference, processing 7B parameter prompts at 40.75 tokens per second. The lack of local storage and GPUs, combined with average multi-core efficiency, positions this instance as a stable, memory-dense resource for enterprise applications where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational speed.
